Yes. I authorize this narrowly scoped exception for the Phase 4 experiment only.

Replies authored by me in this chat may serve as manual founder direction and may be relayed verbatim into content-bound decision records. Those records must preserve the exact source text, timestamp, conversation reference, scope, and decision status.

This is manual founder direction—not cryptographic founder authentication.

Therefore:

* The runtime must refuse every unauthenticated command.
* No chat message may be treated as proof of cryptographic identity.
* Content hashes, signatures, or record integrity must not be represented as founder authentication.
* Manual relay may authorize experimental design and development artifacts only; it may not directly authorize runtime execution.
* No authority, credential, policy, constitutional rule, budget, identity, legal principal, external effect, financial action, publication, outreach, deployment, or recursive self-modification may be created or changed through this exception.
* The experiment remains consequence-inert, proposal-only, and limited to the authorized Phase 4 draft branch.
* The inability to run pytest must remain recorded as an evidence gap. No test success may be claimed until the required environment is available and the tests actually pass.
* Any ambiguity, scope expansion, or conflict must pause and return NEEDS_FOUNDER_DECISION.

This exception does not resolve the founder-authentication gap, waive the requirement for real cryptographic authentication, or authorize production use. It is valid only for manually relaying my explicit founder direction into the content-bound records of this experiment.

Proceed within these limits. Stop and return for a new founder ruling before merge, deployment, activation, external consequence, live credentials, or any expansion beyond this Phase 4 experiment.

implementation_note: Record-only evidence. The source authoring timestamp and opaque conversation/message IDs are not exposed by this interface; null is not replaced with a guessed timestamp or ID. recorded_at is the observed relay time, not the authored time.
